text:
alex: hey DX team — I'm walking through the Go SDK sample that combines generator + streaming and hit a weird auth/retry + ctx interaction. Repro summary: auth refresh happens mid-stream, Recv/Next never returns and goroutines pile up. Anyone run into this?

josh: yikes. do you have a minimal repro or logs?

alex: here's the simplified pattern from the sample:```
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
defer cancel()
gen := client.Generator(ctx, req)
for gen.Next() {
  tok := gen.Recv() // blocks when transport errors happen
  _ = tok
}
if err := gen.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("gen err: %v", err) }
```
The stack shows the goroutine stuck in Recv after a transport-level Unauthenticated, and Next() never returns false.

sara: are you using the low-level streaming Recv API or the iterator helper? semantics differ right now.

alex: iterator helper (Next/Recv/Err). the sample uses that because it's supposed to be ergonomic for newbies.

kai: which SDK version? any auth middleware in front?

alex: v0.7.1, using default auth provider. logs: "auth: refresh started" -> "rpc error: code = Unauthenticated desc = token expired" -> then silence from the generator side.

lisa: i've seen this pattern. root cause: transport-level refresh causes an error that we bubble up in one layer but we don't properly signal the iterator to terminate. the internal receive goroutine is left waiting on a recv from a closed/errored stream.

josh: proposed fix: when we hit Unauthenticated we should set an internal closing flag + cancel the stream ctx, ensure Recv returns an error and Next() returns false. add a defensive recv timeout in the sample.

alex: also the onboarding README currently shows examples with context.Background() w/o cancellation guidance. users copy that and leak. we should update the sample to show ctx.WithCancel and call cancel on errors or on program shutdown.

sara: agree. other idea: provide a GeneratorWithRecovery helper that attempts auth refresh + transparent reconnect for common cases and only surfaces a fatal error if recovery fails. document semantics clearly.

kai: +1. i'll open an issue and a PR: update sample, add test that simulates auth mid-stream and assert Next() returns false and Err() is set. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: created issue #4521 (devex: generator stream auth midstream leak)

alex: thanks! one more small doc ask — add a short "detecting mid-stream auth failures" pattern in devdocs. sample snippet with select on ctx.Done() + stream.Err() will help callers avoid blocky loops.

lisa: i'll draft the devdoc and the sample patch. tagging @eng-ml for API preference if we add GeneratorWithRecovery.

alex: great, appreciate it. :eyes:
